sections.content: Specialised Spanish builds many of its terms from a root plus a suffix, so a reader who knows the root and the suffix can decode most technical words. You know some of these pairs already (*crecer → crecimiento*, *organizar → organización*, *rico → enriquecer*); this lesson shows the system behind them. Nouns come from verbs and adjectives. Verbs come from nouns and adjectives. And some verbs are built on both sides at once, with a prefix before the root and a suffix after it.

sections.title: Nouns from verbs and adjectives
rows: -ción: the action or its result (to ferment → fermentation)
-miento: the action or its result (to grow → growth)
-ura: a quality or a measure (high → height)
-ización: from a verb in -izar (to organise → organisation)

sections.title: Verbs from nouns and adjectives
rows: -izar: to make, to turn into (to stabilise)
-ecer: to become, to make (to get dark)

items.spanish: El calor acelera la fermentación de la mezcla.
items.english: Heat speeds up the fermentation of the mixture.

items.spanish: Hay que estabilizar la temperatura antes de empezar.
items.english: You have to stabilise the temperature before starting.

items.spanish: Ensanchamos la ventana para ver mejor.
items.english: We widened the window to see better.

items.spanish: Los precios bajaron y eso abarató el pan.
items.english: Prices fell and that made bread cheaper.

sections.content: English *-tion* often matches *-ción* (*fermentation → fermentación*), but not always: *growth* is *crecimiento* and *height* is *altura*. Choose the suffix from the Spanish root, not from the English word. A suffix tells you the kind of word, not whether the word exists: *estabilizar* does, but nobody says *estabilizamiento*. Use only words you have met or checked in a dictionary.
